issues.description: The problem statement/UML specifies acceptSupplyDelivery should take four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) with signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int), but the provided solution implements acceptSupplyDelivery with three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity) acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int). This mismatch in method parameters is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students about the required method signature and parameter ordering.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signatures consistent. Either update the solution/template to implement acceptSupplyDelivery with four parameters (String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) — the supplierName can be accepted and ignored if unused — or update the problem statement/UML to specify the three-parameter signature (String ingredientName, int price, int quantity). Preferably, adjust the solution/template to match the problem statement by adding the supplierName parameter so students implement the method exactly as specified.

issues.description: The problem statement/UML describe acceptSupplyDelivery as taking four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) while the provided code (template Main usage and the solution SealSaloon) implements a three-parameter method (ingredient name, price, quantity). This mismatch in the method signature (presence of a separate supplierName parameter in the problem vs. its absence in code) creates confusion for students about the intended API and which parameters they should implement and use.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the API specification and the code. Either update the problem statement/UML to specify a three-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) to match the template/solution, or change the template and solution to implement the four-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (and update usages accordingly). Ensure the chosen signature is reflected consistently in the problem text, UML, template Main, and solution files.
